SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Severe headache for the past four days.
- Associated symptoms: Reported feeling hot and possibly febrile (fever not objectively measured), general muscle aching (not localized to neck), feeling cold at times, new red itchy rash that blanches under pressure (described as all over body), recent history of travel to Thailand (approximately one week ago), received typical mosquito bites during travel.
- Headache history: Headache started before fever. No photophobia, no neck stiffness or pain on neck movement, no vomiting, no cough or cold symptoms, no earache, no pins and needles, no focal weakness.
- Friend who traveled with patient has also become unwell.
- Past medical history: Denied any chronic medical conditions or past surgeries.
- Medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented), Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented). Not on other regular medications.
- Allergies: Denied.
- Social history: Recent travel to Thailand, otherwise not detailed.

Objective:
- No examination performed (remote consult).
- No vitals documented.
- Rash: Red, itchy, all-over body, blanches with pressure (“glass test”).
- No mention of bleeding, no non-blanching rash.
- No other objective findings documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Severe headache with fever and myalgia after travel to Thailand:
   - Assessment: Acute headache, fever, myalgia, blanching rash post-travel — possible tropical infection (e.g., viral illness; dengue less likely as no bleeding or non-blanching rash noted); atypical presentation possible; need to rule out meningitis (though no neck stiffness, photophobia, or non-blanching rash).
   - Differential diagnosis: Viral illness, tropical infection (e.g., dengue—less likely), early meningitis (bacterial or viral), other travel-related infections.
   - Investigations planned: Recommendation for urgent in-person assessment and possible blood tests.
   - Treatment planned: Continue supportive care (paracetamol and ibuprofen); no new medications initiated during call.
   - Relevant referrals: Advise urgent review at clinic hub within hours; if not available, attend emergency department for further evaluation.

Quality checks:
●	Missing but clinically expected elements: No vitals, objective fever measurement, detailed travel history (dates, exposures), full review of systems, full social history.
●	Medications: Doses, routes, frequencies not documented for paracetamol or ibuprofen.
●	Internal conflicts: No notable internal conflicts identified.
●	Transcript quality: Clear; no significant inaudible or noisy portions.
